items.critique: Weakest: granularity — bundles four assertions (final == v, intermediate == 0, nonzero-when-v!=0, frame conditions on other balances and live set) into one item. Implementation_readiness/actionability next: names the write-sequence surface but never pins the real failure mode (overflow of bal+v, zero-value pruning deleting the account, dirty-cache staleness), so the auditor must supply it.

Weakest on specificity, implementation_readiness, and actionability: it is a verbatim restatement of a Lean theorem (quantifier over all states M, Distinct predicate) with no code artifact, function, field, or storage location named. No real failure surface — no deletion-vs-zeroing, iteration, or index concern is pinned. Also bundles zeroing, set removal, and a state-quantified corollary.

Weakest on specificity, implementation_readiness and actionability: it restates a Lean-style invariant (L.live/M.bal/Distinct) in prose without naming any code area, data structure, or concrete failure mode (e.g. pruning a zero balance, dust rounding, duplicate insert path). Granularity also suffers: nonzero-implies-membership and list distinctness are two separate invariants bundled together.

Weakest on granularity and specificity: it bundles five separate post-conditions (non-membership, exactly-one deletion, order preservation, distinctness, balance immutability) into one item, and it is a prose transcription of the DETAIL theorem — no function, field, or container type is named, so the auditor must locate the removal path unaided.

Weakest on specificity, implementation_readiness, actionability, and generality: it transcribes a Lean lemma (hN && hN' ==> N.supply + R == N_prime.supply, M.bal s) rather than naming any code path, field, or supply-mutating function. The only implementation hook is "non-wrapping Nat arithmetic," left abstract — no width, no overflow boundary, no operation. An auditor must reconstruct which code this governs before checking anything, and the proof-object names bind it to one formalization.

Weakest is generality: the bal-v/bal+v pre-read pair is a narrow pattern close to a specific stale-read bug shape, though it does abstract to any account-write path. Otherwise strong — exact operand-derivation condition, concrete stale-read failure mode, clear remedy, one concern.

Weakest on specificity and implementation_readiness: it names the invariant and both violation directions crisply, but not the code site (which enumeration/iterator, which delete-on-zero path) or the concrete mechanism — stale index after a zero-write, dirty-set flush ordering, or cached key list not pruned. Auditor must still locate the surface.
